items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Round, ball-shaped flames of ethylene and methane burned in space, with the gas flowing out or in. The tests look for the point where a flame starts to make soot and measure how hot the flame is there. They vary the flow, the added inert gas (nitrogen or carbon dioxide) and the pressure.

items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Methane and ethylene mixed with nitrogen burn on flat round porous burners in still air in space. The aim is to describe when a material burns in calm microgravity in terms of its properties. Oxygen level and pressure are varied, including the atmosphere planned for human missions.

items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Weak methane and ethylene flames burn in a slow stream of air in space. The tests measure flame shape, how far the flame lifts off the burner, temperatures, the point where the flame goes out, and how much soot forms. The data are meant to test computer models of flames.

items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Gas flames burn in space while a strong electric field is applied across them. Without buoyancy, the effect of the field can be seen on its own. The tests link the voltage to the electric current in the flame and watch how the flame and its soot react.

items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments-Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Mixtures of hydrogen, methane and inert gas flow out of a round porous burner in space and burn as a ball-shaped flame. Cameras and sensors record how the flame changes over time. The results are meant to be compared with detailed computer simulations.

items.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
items.hardware_group_label: Flow duct in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
items.summary_plain: Samples of solid material burned in a small wind tunnel inside the space station's glovebox, with astronauts running the tests. The tests study how a flame starts, grows, spreads and goes out in slow airflow. The main things changed are the airflow speed and the oxygen level.

items.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
items.hardware_group_label: Flow duct in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
items.summary_plain: Fabric and plastic samples burned in the glovebox on the space station, in a flow of air. The goal is to close the gap between the standard NASA test for material flammability on the ground and what really happens in microgravity. Thicker, more realistic materials are used.

items.title: Cool Flames Investigation
items.hardware_group_label: Droplet apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Tiny drops of dodecane fuel burn in space in a chamber where pressure and gas mix are controlled. The tests look at cool flames, which burn at low temperature, and how helium in the gas, drop size and pressure change when the flame goes out.

items.title: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test / Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test-2
items.hardware_group_label: Smoke and aerosol instruments
items.summary_plain: A test that checks whether a particle counter changed for space still counts correctly in microgravity before it was used on real smoke. The counter was rebuilt so that it no longer relies on gravity, and a standard dust was blown through it as a reference.

items.title: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
items.hardware_group_label: Ground investigation (re-uses PSI data)
items.summary_plain: A ground study that re-uses the SPICE images. It turns the raw photos into maps of soot temperature and soot amount and compares them with a computer soot model. The aim is to explain why soot forms differently on Earth and in microgravity.

items.title: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography
items.hardware_group_label: Ground investigation (re-uses PSI data)
items.summary_plain: A modeling study of flames that spread along solid material in the same direction as the airflow. It builds a faster computer method and compares it with the BASS experiments on sheets, spheres and PMMA rods.

items.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
items.hardware_group_label: Droplet apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: A follow-up to FLEX that burns droplets of fuel mixtures in space, in atmospheres closer to real engines. Pressure and oxygen level are varied and the rest of the gas is a diluent. The results are meant to check computer models of droplet burning.

items.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
items.hardware_group_label: Droplet apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Large droplets of liquid fuel are lit in space and the oxygen level is lowered until the flame no longer burns. This is repeated with carbon dioxide, helium or SF6 added to find how well each gas puts a fire out. The results feed models of when flames can exist.

items.title: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I
items.hardware_group_label: Saffire enclosure in a Cygnus spacecraft
items.summary_plain: A large sheet of cotton and fiberglass fabric is set on fire inside an unmanned cargo spacecraft after it left the space station. The tests ask how fast a big fire grows in low gravity and how the limits for burning compare with NASA's ground screening test.

items.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
items.hardware_group_label: Saffire enclosure in a Cygnus spacecraft
items.summary_plain: The second large fire test, again run on a cargo spacecraft after it left the station. It adds more materials: fabric, silicone and several kinds of acrylic (PMMA). It asks how fast a large fire grows in low gravity and how burning limits compare with NASA's ground screening test.

items.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
items.hardware_group_label: Saffire enclosure in a Cygnus spacecraft
items.summary_plain: The third large fire test on a cargo spacecraft, using the same fabric as the first. The airflow is faster (30 cm/s instead of 20 cm/s) and runs with or against the flame. It asks how fast a large fire grows in low gravity and how burning limits compare with NASA's ground screening test.

items.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight
items.hardware_group_label: Smoke and aerosol instruments
items.summary_plain: Smoke from heated samples is measured in the space station's glovebox to learn how big the smoke droplets get in low gravity. This repeat flight changed the test material to a fire-retardant foam, widened the heating conditions and swapped one instrument for a new one.

items.title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
items.hardware_group_label: Smoke and aerosol instruments
items.summary_plain: Smoke is made by heating samples in the space station's glovebox, and the size of the smoke droplets is measured. A computer code was also planned to predict how smoke droplets grow. Two smoke detectors and thermal samplers were used.

items.title: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
items.hardware_group_label: Flow duct in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
items.summary_plain: Gas flames from tubes of different sizes burn in a slow airflow in the space station's glovebox. The tests look at how the base of the flame is held in place and at what flow the flame lifts off the burner. Nitrogen is mixed into the fuel to see the effect on soot and stability.

items.title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
items.hardware_group_label: Flow duct in the Microgravity Science Glovebox
items.summary_plain: Small gas flames of methane, ethylene, propane and propylene burn in a flow of air in space. The fuel flow is raised until the flame starts to release smoke, the smoke point. The tests vary burner size and airflow speed.

items.title: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
items.hardware_group_label: Ground investigation (re-uses PSI data)
items.summary_plain: A computer study of how smoke particles form and grow, with and without gravity. It simulates the pyrolysis smoke of the SAME experiments at two slow cross-flow speeds. The aim is to say how microgravity smoke differs from Earth smoke and why.

items.title: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
items.hardware_group_label: Ground investigation (re-uses PSI data)
items.summary_plain: A computer model of cool flames around fuel droplets in microgravity, checked against the FLEX flight data. It tests how added heat and small drifts in the gas change whether a cool flame survives.

items.title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
items.hardware_group_label: Ground investigation (re-uses PSI data)
items.summary_plain: Simulations and ground experiments that use the FLEX conditions to study cool flames, which burn at low temperature. The goal is a new diagram of when such flames can exist and a link between their limits and those of ordinary hot flames.

items.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
items.hardware_group_label: ACME hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack
items.summary_plain: Round gas flames of propane, n-butane and n-pentane are burned in space to find when a cool flame (a faint, low-temperature flame) can exist. The tests vary the fuel, the dilution, the flow and the pressure. Computer simulations support the flight tests.
